title.narrative: Provision of Lifesaving GBV and Child Protection Interventions among Conflict affected Returnees and Refugees in Panakauch – Rubkona, Unity state of South

description.narrative: ltpgtWART is proposing a lifesaving protection response to address GBV and Child protection emerging problems among returnees and refugees in Panakuach Payam. In line with 2025 SSHF RA1, WART confirms influx of returnees and refugees emanating from conflict dynamic of Sudan crisis. Women, girls, and children have been displaced and forced to flee into Unity State settling in Panakuach Payam. This has resulted into a surge in GBV incident reports and child separation and it is feared that this could escalate even further to a life threating situation.ltbrgtIn the event that the current CP and GBV needs in Panakuach escalate further, which is highly likely as no response is currently being undertaken, WART through the proposed SSHF RA1 strategy will provide GBV and child protection activities and scale up to tackle underlying issues that drive GBV and CP issues so as to reduce vulnerability of women, girls and boys among Returnees and Refugees in Panakuach affected by protracted conflictltbrgtThe project will reach 4,000 vulnerable populations comprising 2,500 returnees and 1,500 Refugees with the following activities.ltbrgt Increase access to protection services and reduce vulnerability and suffering of girls, boys, women, men, who experience GBV violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect, ensuring that all efforts are geared towards reducing vulnerability and risks for Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV), ltbrgt Scale-up life-saving protection services for both, female and male GBV survivors and community members at high risk of GBV, ltbrgt Provide Capacity building within the community to support the provision of quality and comprehensive case management services through community-based approachesltbrgt Conduct identification of protection concerns and referrals through static or mobile means, Protection Risk Monitoring, ltbrgt Conduct Protection awareness raising and messaging on GBV risks, available response services and timely reportingltbrgt Provide Cash and voucher assistance support, ltbrgt Conduct Distribution of dignity kits, ltbrgt Provide specialized case management, provide GBV response services, referrals, PSS WGFS programming ltbrgt Provide family tracing and reunification of unaccompanied and separated children and train staff on Child Protection in Emergencies (CPiE), and GBV response child and adolescent-friendly spaces, parenting skill sessions with caregivers, life skills sessions, Peer-to-peer support activities with children and adolescents.ltbrgtThe project implementation strategies will include capacity development for sustainability protection programming area-based development approach Do no harm, conﬂict sensitivity planning, AAP and feedback mechanisms, and gender and youth mainstreaming and empowerment. Further WART will make effort to avoid exposing beneficiaries and staff to further harm as a result of addressing protection concerns that may be caused or exacerbated by the humanitarian response and thus WART will apply its safeguarding policy to ensure protection of beneficiaries. WART will ensure implementation of the protection response is well coordinated with GBV AoR sub cluster which will provide 400 dignity kits. WART protection officers will brief the community stakeholders about protection issues and assessments to understand the local context to avoid any harm resulting from this project intervention. A complaints desk will be established in schools, CFS, and WGFS, and focused group discussions will be conducted with selected beneficiaries and community leaders for complaints and feedback.ltbrgtIn the proposed intervention, WART will also ensure that, the GBV and CP activities are integrated with other cluster projects such as FSL, CCCM, WASH and Shelter/NFIs, Nutrition, and Education by linking with the partners and ensuring that protection beneficiaries targeted by WART are linked to other partners for them to gain from a wholistic approach of the response. Currently, WART has not secured any funds for the Sudan crisis from other donorsltbrgtlt/pgt
